steps.label: The shared characteristic
steps.margin_note: The shared property plus the word fermentation.
lines: Each of them is used industrially to produce a
steps.why: All three convert a cheap sugar substrate into an acid, which is why they are grouped together despite being a fungus and two bacteria.
common_mistakes: Saying they are all bacteria. Aspergillus niger is a FUNGUS.
Saying they all make the same acid. Each makes a DIFFERENT one.
steps.memory_tip: Three organisms, three acids, one shared job.

steps.label: Which acid each makes
steps.margin_note: All three pairs, and the naming clue. Six lines.
lines: ASPERGILLUS NIGER, a fungus, produces CITRIC
ACID. In each case the name of the acid is a clue to the
name of the organism, or the other way round.
steps.why: Two of the three names carry their product — butylicum gives butyric acid and Lactobacillus gives lactic acid — which makes them easy to keep apart.
common_mistakes: Matching the wrong acid to the wrong organism. Aspergillus is CITRIC, Clostridium butylicum is BUTYRIC, Lactobacillus is LACTIC.
Naming only the acids. Each acid must be matched to its organism.
steps.memory_tip: Butylicum makes butyric; Lactobacillus makes lactic.
